description: Amends OCP, rezones 702 and 706 Victoria Avenue.
Permits six-story building instead of four stories.

chips.text: First reading passed (9-0)
9 for, 0 against
Councillor Dubois questioned short-term rental rules and unit ownership.
Marr Residence, a national historic site, is adjacent to the property.
Public concerns raised about local traffic, rear lane use, and construction impacts.
Shadow studies showed minimal additional impact on Marr Residence from extra stories.

speakers.name: James Peirce
speakers.summary: James Peirce, Kindrachuk Agrey Architecture, addressed the matter using a PowerPoint presentation on building height limits, massing, and the shadow study’s impact on the neighbouring Marr Residence.
said: Proposed six-story building with beautiful design.
Completes high-density corner; minimal height increase.
Shadow studies show minimal impact on heritage residence.

description: Proposes rezoning 702 and 706 Victoria Avenue to high-density.

Zoning agreement specifies building height, setbacks, and short-term rentals.

chips.text: First reading passed (9-0)
9 for, 0 against
No public speakers addressed Council regarding this rezoning application.

description: Allows two-story garden/garage suites city-wide with rear lane access.
Removes neighborhood categories restricting two-story suites.
Permits up to four units on 15-meter wide sites.

chips.text: First reading passed (9-0)
9 for, 0 against
Councillor Donauer asked about future infill barriers; Ms. Burgess cited site coverage.
Residents in Category 2 neighborhoods like Mayfair and Forest Grove are impacted.
A delegate questioned if the amendment was needed to increase missing middle housing supply.
Home Builders' Association supported infill; a delegate opposed, citing homeowner rights.
Not meeting conditions could lead to CMHC scrutiny for Housing Accelerator Fund.
Concerns raised about 0.75-meter path width for wheelchair accessibility.
Administration will bring primary dwelling amendments to Council in July.

speakers.name: Sherry Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Sherry Tarasoff, via teleconference, presented a video expressing opposition and raised concerns regarding accessibility and homeowner rights.
said: Massing controls seem eliminated, removing homeowner protection.
Proposed 0.75m path width is insufficient for wheelchair access.
Missing middle housing targets were already exceeded in 2024.

speakers.name: Nicole Burgess
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Zoning Bylaw Text Amendmts – Garden and Garage Suites
said: Amendments remove barriers, improve consistency, and create housing opportunities.
Current regulations hinder infill; only 9.5% of development was infill.
Extending two-story suites to Category 2 neighborhoods ensures consistency.

description: Permits six-unit dwellings on corner lots in transit areas.

chips.text: First reading passed (9-0)
9 for, 0 against
Councillors debated density on corner lots, parking rules, and affordable housing impacts.
Residents in the Transit Development Area may see more six-unit buildings.
This discretionary use could eventually become permitted, like secondary suites.
Councillor Pierce questioned if the changes ensure affordable housing.
